api_reference: The learner writes JavaScript for a tiny scene API. Only these functions exist: ground(color), tree(x, z, size?), rock(x, z, size?), house(x, z, size?), sun(height 0..90), fog(amount 0..1), random(min, max). x and z are in -20..20, size in 0.3..4. At most 400 objects. Nothing else (no DOM, no network, no other globals).

lessons.concept: A command call needs concrete numbers for its arguments.
typical_gaps: the tree line is still commented out with //
x and z were left as letters instead of numbers
the call is missing parentheses, comma or semicolon

lessons.concept: A for loop repeats a block; the loop variable can drive positions; the loop condition sets how many turns.
typical_gaps: trees were typed one by one instead of in a loop
the loop condition i < N gives fewer turns than needed
every tree has the same z so the forest is a single row
random() is used for x only

lessons.concept: sun(height) and fog(amount) set mood; lower sun means warmer light; the scale of each argument matters.
goals: Lower the sun to 15 or less
Raise the fog to 0.3 or more
typical_gaps: sun() was never called so the light stays at midday
sun() value is still above 15 (90 is overhead, 0 is the horizon)
fog() is missing or too faint
fog was given a value above 1

lessons.concept: Combine loops, placement and atmosphere into an original scene; composition matters (spacing, grouping, variety).
typical_gaps: not enough houses, trees or rocks yet
houses stand on one straight line
no loop used for repeated objects
